summary: POC scoping focused on integration approach for Cygnus's pipeline: OpenAI-compatible endpoints, SDK usage, function/tool-calling, structured JSON outputs, success criteria (latency, accuracy, cost), workload sizing and benchmark plan, and timelines for a 4-week POC.
meeting_header: Date: 2027-08-04 | Time: 4:00 PM PDT | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Maya Chen; Diego Alvarez; Priya Shah; Liam O'Connor; Aisha Bello
transcript: 00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you taking the time. I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood side, bringing Diego our SE for the integration details. 00:07 Priya Shah: Hi Maya, thanks. We wanted to make sure we cover integration details - SDK experience and what success looks like for the POC. 00:15 Diego Alvarez: Great, quick agenda: go through success criteria, sizing, benchmarks, then deep dive on integration: SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function calling and structured outputs. 00:25 Aisha Bello: Sounds good. We're mainly evaluating latency impact for customer-facing features and how easy it is to map our tooling to Redwood's API. 00:33 Maya Chen: Perfect, can you share a quick baseline - current stack and volumes? 00:37 Priya Shah: Sure. We run most inference in house on k8s, model calls are about 200 QPS at peak for our conversational summarization flow, average request length 600 tokens, response about 120 tokens, so fairly steady. Also about 30k monthly long-form batch jobs. 00:52 Liam O'Connor: Infrastructure wise we have GCP, use VPC peering for some partners, and strict data residency for EU customers. We prefer private deployments for PII workloads but can use hosted for lower-sensitivity flows. 01:05 Diego Alvarez: That's helpful - so success criteria from Redwood perspective usually break into: latency SLOs (p95 under X ms), quality/regression metrics (per prompt evals), and cost per 1k tokens. What are your target numbers? 01:20 Priya Shah: For the interactive feature we need p95 < 350ms and average TTFB under 150ms. Accuracy: our rouge/f1 on summarization should not drop more than 2% compared to our current baseline. Cost: we'd like to understand the delta - if cost increases by > 30% that's a blocker. 01:37 Maya Chen: Noted. We can run a benchmark: Redwood Dedicated and hosted variants, measure cold vs warm KV cache, batching impacts, plus quantized model variants. Diego will run perf scripts with your sample traffic. 01:50 Priya Shah: On integration, key question: do you support OpenAI-compatible endpoints so our existing SDKs need minimal changes? 01:56 Diego Alvarez: Yes - we provide an OpenAI-compatible API layer for text generation and chat; it supports same-ish request/response shapes, and we also have our native SDKs in Python and Node. There are some Redwood-specific fields for routing and cache hints but those are optional. 02:10 Aisha Bello: And function calling / tool calling - we use it heavily to trigger retrieval and downstream actions. Is that supported? 02:16 Diego Alvarez: Absolutely - we support function/tool calling patterns. You can register schemas and Redwood will forward structured outputs or call hooks. The transcripts from our labs show structured JSON output support and we can route model responses to your microservices. 02:28 Priya Shah: The structured outputs are critical - we need stable JSON schema so our parsers don't break. How do you guarantee schema adherence? 02:35 Diego Alvarez: Couple of levers: 1) we have structured output mode with strict decoding and validation; 2) a post-processing resin layer can reject/repair outputs; 3) we recommend evals against a seed set and Redwood Optimize can alert on schema drift. Note sometimes the transcriptions in our logs say "Redwood Dedicate" which is a weird artifact but the functionality is stable, just FYI. 02:56 Maya Chen: For SDKs, we can share code snippets - the Python SDK call is like existing OpenAI usage, e.g. client.chat.create with model parameter. We also expose low-level REST. 03:08 Liam O'Connor: Any client TLS/KMS integrations for key management? We have to support CMEK for EU data. 03:13 Diego Alvarez: Yes we integrate with major KMS/HSM providers and support customer-managed keys for Private deployments. For hosted we offer KMS integrations but would need an enterprise agreement for CMEK. 03:24 Priya Shah: Benchmarks - what's the plan? 03:26 Diego Alvarez: We'll do staged runs: synthetic traffic matching your QPS and token distributions, then a representative run using your sample dataset. We'll capture latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput, token cost, and failure rates. We'll test three deployment modes: hosted, dedicated reserved pool, and private. We'll also profile with warm KV cache and cold starts. 03:44 Priya Shah: How long will benchmarking take? 03:46 Diego Alvarez: End-to-end we expect to coordinate a 48-72 hour benchmark window plus time to analyze. Practically, schedule ~1 week to set up creds and get the sample data in. 03:55 Maya Chen: Timeline for a POC - what does your team recommend? 03:58 Diego Alvarez: Typical is 4 weeks: week 0 onboarding + infra setup, week 1-2 benchmarking and integration, week 3 accuracy/regression evals, week 4 finalize roll decision and handoff docs. If you want a gated canary we can extend. 04:12 Aisha Bello: For onboarding, how do we wire function calls to our retrieval? Do you have webhook hooks or do we pull? 04:18 Diego Alvarez: We support both: synchronous tool calling via webhook and an async queue pattern. For low-latency actions we recommend direct sync webhooks with retries and idempotency tokens. 04:30 Priya Shah: Any gotchas we should know - rate limits, batching behavior affecting latency? 04:35 Diego Alvarez: Yes batching helps cost but can add tail latency depending on your traffic pattern; we can tune per-route batching windows. Also KV cache warmup is important for large prefix reuse. We'll give a KB doc with best-practices. 04:50 Liam O'Connor: Regarding network, for private deployments will we need to set up a private endpoint in our VPC? 04:55 Diego Alvarez: For Private we provide a customer-controlled VPC endpoint and an on-prem package if needed. We'll share the VPC peering checklist. 05:03 Priya Shah: For success criteria recap: p95 < 350ms, accuracy within -2% of baseline, cost delta < +30%, and no data leakage for EU PII flows. 05:14 Maya Chen: Good, we'll capture that in the POC charter. We'll also include rollback criteria and acceptance tests. 05:20 Aisha Bello: Can you show us a quick code snippet of the SDK mapping to our current OpenAI calls? 05:25 Diego Alvarez: Sure, quick example: (diego types) client = RedwoodClient(...); response = client.chat.create({"model": "rwd-compact-1","messages": [...] , "function_call": {"name": "fetch_docs"}}) and the response will include a structured function_call payload you can wire to your retrieval layer. 05:45 Priya Shah: Great - minor transcription: sometimes "model rwd-compact" gets misheard in notes as "our compact model" but that's fine. 05:51 Maya Chen: Next steps recap: I'll send the integration guide and pricing, Diego will send benchmark plan and perf script, Liam will provide VPC/test creds, Priya will share sample prompts and eval criteria. 06:00 Priya Shah: Ok we'll aim to have the sample set by Tuesday the 9th. Thanks. 06:06 Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with a calendar invite for the benchmark window. 06:10 [meeting ends]
